```{r, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
options(width = 76)
# A figure whose pixels are all opaque is written without its alpha channel:
# the same pixels in a smaller file.
opaque_png <- function(path) {
  x <- png::readPNG(path)
  if (length(dim(x)) == 3 && dim(x)[3] == 4 && all(x[, , 4] == 1)) {
    png::writePNG(x[, , 1:3], path)
  }
  path
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4.4, out.width = "100%", dpi = 117,
                      fig.process = if (requireNamespace("png", quietly = TRUE)) opaque_png)
```

`evaluate_array()` runs a whole simulation in one call. This page runs it one step at a time,
from tracks to location surfaces and scores. Figure 1 is the location surface of one
animal-hour, which section 6 builds step by step.

```{r opening-surface, echo = FALSE, purl = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.height = 5.4, fig.alt = "Location surface of one animal-hour on Stoney Lake in magma colours over water drawn by depth, with its 95% region outlined, three yellow rings for the receivers that heard the animal, white rings for silent receivers, and the animal's true transmissions as green points and red crosses."}
# Draw the map of section 6 as a preview from evaluate_array(); the code is
# shown there
library(ggplot2)
eval(parse(text = knitr::knit_code$get("surface-map-helper")))
hero_lake <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                     package = "arraydesign"))
hero_receivers <- arraydesign::place_receivers(
  terra::ifel(abs(hero_lake) < 1, NA, hero_lake), n = 20, method = "grid",
  seed = 1
)
hero_model <- detfield::de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500),
                                    depth = c(1, 35))
hero_eval <- arraydesign::evaluate_array(
  hero_receivers, hero_lake, hero_model, n_animals = 20,
  seed = 1, control = list(hours = 6, tag_delay = c(120, 180))
)
hero_overall <- hero_eval$score$overall
hero_detections <- hero_eval$detections$detections
hero_detections$bin_start <- as.POSIXct(
  floor(as.numeric(hero_detections$datetime) / 3600) * 3600,
  origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"
)
hero_heard_by <- aggregate(receiver_serial ~ animal_id + bin_start,
                           data = hero_detections,
                           FUN = function(serials) length(unique(serials)))
hero_ties <- merge(
  hero_heard_by[hero_heard_by$receiver_serial ==
                  max(hero_heard_by$receiver_serial), ],
  hero_eval$score$bins[c("animal_id", "bin_start", "n_truth", "in_region")]
)
hero_hour <- hero_ties[which.min(abs(hero_ties$in_region -
                                       hero_overall$hit_rate)), ]
surface_map(hero_eval$surfaces, hero_hour$animal_id, hero_hour$bin_start,
            hero_lake, hero_receivers, hero_eval$detections$detections,
            hero_eval$detections$transmissions)
```

*Figure 1. The location surface of one animal-hour of the reference run of `evaluate_array()`
(20 animals over 6 hours) on the 20-receiver grid, rebuilt step by step in section 6, with the
animal's true transmissions in the hour.*

The 95% region of an hourly surface holds a moving animal about half the time. The hit rate of
this run, which averages over animal-hours the share of each hour's true positions inside its
region, is `r sprintf("%.3f", hero_overall$hit_rate)`, because the surface treats the animal as
still for the hour while it swims about `r sprintf("%.1f", 30 * 60 / 1000)` km. In the hour
mapped, `r round(hero_hour$in_region * hero_hour$n_truth)` of the animal's
`r hero_hour$n_truth` true positions lie inside the region.

Each step below returns a table you can inspect, change or pass to your own code. Sections 4 and
5 add receivers that stop listening part way through, and detection that varies from hour to
hour. This page's code is included as `simulate-detections.R` in
`system.file("scripts", package = "arraydesign")`.

The lake, the array and the range model are those of [Get started](arraydesign.html): Stoney
Lake at 100 m, the 20-receiver grid, and the example's assumed range model. The first step
loads the packages, reads the lake and lays the grid.

```{r set-up-the-array}
# Load the package, and ggplot2 for the maps
library(arraydesign)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the depth raster of Stoney Lake
lake <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                package = "arraydesign"))

# Lay a grid of 20 receivers over water at least 1 m deep
deployable <- terra::ifel(abs(lake) < 1, NA, lake)
receivers <- place_receivers(deployable, n = 20, method = "grid", seed = 1)
nrow(receivers)
```

The range model is `detfield::de_logistic()`, which serves when no range test exists, and
the detection field holds one probability per receiver and water cell.

```{r detection-field}
# Set the assumed d50 and d05 for receivers 1 m and 35 m deep
range_model <- detfield::de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500),
                                     depth = c(1, 35))

# Build the field: distances through water, then the curve at each
# distance and depth
field <- detfield::de_field(detfield::water_distances(lake, receivers),
                            range_model)

# Print the column that names the receivers of the field
field$key
```

The field is keyed by station, because the receivers have a `station_id`.

## 1. Tracks

The tracks are those of the reference run in the
[**arraydesignR**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/arraydesignR/) R package, **arraydesign** in
a browser: 20 animals for 6 hours (360 steps of 60 s) from midnight UTC,
under the correlated random walk of [Specifying and testing movement models](movement-models.html).
The print gives the steps taken as drawn and reflected at the shore, and the first positions.

```{r simulate-tracks}
# Build a walk: gamma steps of mean 30 m a minute, turns of sd 40 degrees
walk <- crw_model(step_mean = 30, step_sd = 15, turn_sd = 40, time_step_s = 60)

# Walk 20 animals for 360 steps of 60 s from midnight UTC
start <- as.POSIXct("2025-01-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")
tracks <- simulate_tracks(lake, walk, n_animals = 20, n_steps = 360,
                          control = track_control(start_time = start),
                          seed = 1)
tracks
```

## 2. Transmissions

Each animal's tag transmits with a random delay of 120 to 180 s, a mean of 24 an hour. The
chunk returns one row per transmission.

```{r simulate-transmissions}
# Send a transmission every 120 to 180 s along each track
transmissions <- simulate_transmissions(tracks, tag_delay = c(120, 180),
                                        seed = 1)
head(transmissions)

# Count the transmissions in all, and per animal-hour
nrow(transmissions)
nrow(transmissions) / (20 * 6)
```

## 3. Detections

Each receiver of the field has one chance to detect each transmission, with the probability the
field gives for the cell the transmission was sent from. The example's assumed range model has
no spread from hour to hour, so the trials are independent (`overdispersion = "none"`).

```{r simulate-detections}
# Give each receiver one trial per transmission
sim <- simulate_detections(transmissions, field, overdispersion = "none",
                           seed = 1)
sim
```

`sim$detections` has the columns of a real detection file. `sim$transmissions` keeps the truth:
every transmission, where it was sent from, and how many receivers heard it. The next chunk
gives, per animal, the share of transmissions heard by at least one receiver.

```{r detection-rate-per-animal}
# Take every transmission, with the number of receivers that heard it
truth <- sim$transmissions

# Compute the share of each animal's transmissions heard by any receiver
rate <- tapply(truth$n_detections > 0, truth$path_id, mean)
round(rate, 3)

# Give the mean, standard error and median across animals, and the
# animals never heard
c(mean = mean(rate), se = sd(rate) / sqrt(length(rate)), median = median(rate))
sum(rate == 0)
```

These rates match
[step 4 of Get started](arraydesign.html#simulate-animals-and-their-detections) and the app's
Simulation tab. An animal-hour with no detection cannot be positioned; the
next chunk counts those that have one.

```{r animal-hours-heard}
# Find the hour of the run in which each transmission was sent, 0 to 5
hour_of_run <- floor(as.numeric(truth$datetime - start, units = "hours"))

# Find the animal-hours with at least one detection, as a share of all 120
heard_hours <- unique(data.frame(path_id = truth$path_id,
                                 hour = hour_of_run)[truth$n_detections > 0, ])
nrow(heard_hours) / (20 * 6)
```

These are the animal-hours that `evaluate_array()` scores in
[step 5 of Get started](arraydesign.html#score-positions). Figure 2 maps the north-east basin,
where the heard transmissions lie close to the receivers.

```{r map-detected-transmissions, fig.alt = "Close-up of the north-east basin of Stoney Lake: pale grey tracks with white start points, green heard transmissions near the receivers, small red crosses along the tracks elsewhere."}
# Take the water cells, with depth as positive metres
water <- terra::as.data.frame(lake, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
names(water)[3] <- "depth_m"
water$depth_m <- abs(water$depth_m)

# Convert the tracks to a plain table
paths <- as.data.frame(tracks)[c("path_id", "x", "y")]

# Map the tracks, misses, heard transmissions, the starts (the first
# position of each track) and receivers over the basin. The colour scale keys
# the tracks and transmissions; the shape scale keys the receivers, a dark
# ring under a coloured one
ring <- detfield::positionr_ring_colours()
ggplot(water, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = depth_m)) +
  detfield::scale_fill_depth() +
  geom_path(data = paths, aes(group = path_id, colour = "Track"),
            linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = truth[truth$n_detections == 0, ], aes(colour = "Not heard"),
             shape = 4, size = 0.8, stroke = 0.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = truth[truth$n_detections > 0, ], aes(colour = "Heard"),
             shape = 21, fill = "#2ECC40", size = 1.8, stroke = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = paths[!duplicated(paths$path_id), ], aes(colour = "Start"),
             shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2, stroke = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = NULL, breaks = c("Track", "Start", "Heard", "Not heard"),
    values = c(Track = "grey85", Start = "black", Heard = "black",
               `Not heard` = "red3"),
    # The key draws the cross larger than the map does, so that it reads
    guide = guide_legend(position = "bottom",
                         override.aes = list(size = c(1, 2, 1.8, 1.6),
                                             stroke = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.3, 0.6),
                                             alpha = 1))
  ) +
  geom_point(data = receivers, aes(shape = "Receiver"), colour = ring[["edge"]],
             size = 4, stroke = 2.2) +
  geom_point(data = receivers, aes(shape = "Receiver"), colour = ring[["heard"]],
             size = 4, stroke = 1.1) +
  scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, values = c(Receiver = 21)) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(730300, 737100), ylim = c(4937700, 4941940),
              expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)") +
  detfield::annotation_scale_bar(location = "br") +
  detfield::theme_positionr()
```

*Figure 2. Tracks and transmissions of the 20 simulated animals of the reference run over 6
hours, in the north-east basin of Stoney Lake.*

## 4. Receivers that stop listening

When the field is built from a deployments table with `deploy_datetime` and `recover_datetime`, a
station makes a trial only while a receiver is in the water there. Here the receiver at S016,
the deepest station of the array, is recovered three hours into the run.

```{r deployments-table}
# Put every receiver in the water from a day before the run to a day after
deployments <- data.frame(receiver_serial = receivers$receiver_serial,
                          station_id = receivers$station_id,
                          x = receivers$x, y = receivers$y,
                          deploy_z = receivers$deploy_z,
                          deploy_datetime = start - 86400,
                          recover_datetime = start + 86400)

# Recover the receiver at S016 three hours into the run
recovered <- deployments$station_id == "S016"
deployments$recover_datetime[recovered] <- start + 3 * 3600
deployments[recovered, c("station_id", "deploy_z", "deploy_datetime",
                         "recover_datetime")]
```

The same transmissions are simulated again under a field built from the deployments, with the
same seed, so the two runs differ only where the field differs.

```{r receiver-recovered-early}
# Build the field from the deployments, then simulate with the same
# transmissions and seed
field_recovered <- detfield::de_field(
  detfield::water_distances(lake, deployments), range_model
)
sim_recovered <- simulate_detections(transmissions, field_recovered,
                                     overdispersion = "none", seed = 1)
```

The message counts the trials not made. The detections at S016 in the two runs:

```{r detections-at-s016}
# Count the detections at S016, listening for 6 hours and recovered at
# 3 hours
c(listening_6_hours = sum(sim$detections$station_id == "S016"),
  recovered_at_3_hours = sum(sim_recovered$detections$station_id == "S016"))
```

## 5. Detection that varies from hour to hour

Range tests often vary more from hour to hour than a binomial allows: a receiver hears well in
one hour and badly in the next, for every animal at once. `detfield::de_model()` adds that spread
as a standard deviation on the logit scale for each station and hour. The value of 1 below is
assumed; no range test of the example measured it.

```{r hourly-spread}
# Add a station-hour sd of 1 on the logit scale to the range model
spread_model <- detfield::de_model(range_model, sigma = list(station_hour = 1))

# Build its detection field
field_spread <- detfield::de_field(detfield::water_distances(lake, receivers),
                                   spread_model)
```

`simulate_detections()` draws the spread by default. The table compares the detection rate per
animal with and without it.

```{r detections-with-spread}
# Simulate with the same transmissions and seed, with the spread drawn
sim_spread <- simulate_detections(transmissions, field_spread, seed = 1)

# Compare the detection rate per animal, without and with the spread
rate_spread <- tapply(sim_spread$transmissions$n_detections > 0,
                      sim_spread$transmissions$path_id, mean)
round(rbind(static = summary(rate), with_spread = summary(rate_spread)), 3)
```

The spread leaves the mean detection rate per animal almost unchanged
(`r sprintf("%.3f", mean(rate_spread))` against `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(rate))`) and widens the
range across animals (highest `r sprintf("%.3f", max(rate_spread))` against
`r sprintf("%.3f", max(rate))`).

## 6. Counts, location surfaces and scores

The [**detfield**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/) R package takes the simulated
detections as it takes real ones. The first step is a listening
table: when each receiver was in the water.

```{r listening-table}
# Set every receiver listening from a day before the run to a day after
listening <- data.frame(receiver_serial = receivers$receiver_serial,
                        station_id = receivers$station_id,
                        deploy_datetime = start - 86400,
                        recover_datetime = start + 86400)
```

`detfield::bin_detections()` counts the detections per animal, receiver and hour, given when
each receiver listened. `y` is the detections and `n` the transmissions expected in the hour.

```{r bin-detections}
# Count the detections per animal, receiver and hour
counts <- detfield::bin_detections(sim$detections, listening,
                                   tag_delay = c(120, 180))
head(counts)
```

`detfield::location_surface()` turns the counts into the probability that the animal was in each
water cell, one surface per animal-hour.

```{r location-surfaces}
# Compute one surface per animal-hour with a detection
surfaces <- detfield::location_surface(counts, field, overdispersion = "none")
```

`score_surfaces()` measures the surfaces against the true transmissions. It scores any surfaces
whose true positions you know, such as those of a range model you fitted with other settings.

```{r score-surfaces}
# Score the error and hit rate of each surface against the truth
score <- score_surfaces(surfaces, truth)
score
head(score$bins[c("animal_id", "bin_start", "n_truth", "error_mean_m",
                  "in_region", "area_m2")])
```

Figure 1 maps one animal-hour. The next chunk picks it: of the animal-hours heard by the most
receivers, the one whose share of true positions inside its 95% region is nearest the run's hit
rate.

```{r pick-the-mapped-hour}
# Count the receivers that heard each animal-hour
heard_by <- aggregate(y ~ animal_id + bin_start, data = counts,
                      FUN = function(detections) sum(detections > 0))
names(heard_by)[3] <- "receivers_heard"

# Find the animal-hours heard by the most receivers, with their scores
most_heard <- merge(
  heard_by[heard_by$receivers_heard == max(heard_by$receivers_heard), ],
  score$bins[c("animal_id", "bin_start", "n_truth", "error_mean_m",
               "in_region")]
)
most_heard

# Pick the one nearest the run's hit rate
mapped_hour <- most_heard[which.min(abs(most_heard$in_region -
                                          score$overall$hit_rate)), ]
mapped_hour
```

`surface_map()` is a page helper that draws one location surface over the lake with the
receivers and the animal's true transmissions in the hour.

```{r surface-map-helper}
# Map one animal-hour: water by depth, the surface in magma from 0 to its
# largest cell, the 95% region outlined, receivers that heard the animal as
# yellow rings sized by their detections, silent receivers as white rings,
# and the animal's true transmissions in the hour, keyed with the outline
surface_map <- function(surfaces, animal, hour, lake, receivers, detections,
                        truth, margin = 500) {
  # Take the cells of the one surface, with their coordinates
  hour_cells <- surfaces[surfaces$animal_id == animal &
                           surfaces$bin_start == hour, ]
  hour_cells <- cbind(hour_cells, terra::xyFromCell(lake, hour_cells$cell))

  # Outline its 95% region
  region <- detfield::credible_region(surfaces, level = 0.95)
  region <- region[region$animal_id == animal & region$bin_start == hour, ]
  outline <- terra::rast(lake)
  outline[region$cell] <- 1
  outline <- terra::geom(terra::as.polygons(outline), df = TRUE)

  # Take the true transmissions and detections of the animal in the hour
  in_hour <- function(times) times >= hour & times < hour + 3600
  hour_truth <- truth[truth$animal_id == animal & in_hour(truth$datetime), ]
  hour_detections <- detections[detections$animal_id == animal &
                                  in_hour(detections$datetime), ]

  # Count the detections per receiver in the hour
  rings <- data.frame(receiver_serial = receivers$receiver_serial,
                      x = receivers$x, y = receivers$y)
  rings$n <- as.vector(table(factor(hour_detections$receiver_serial,
                                    levels = rings$receiver_serial)))
  heard <- rings[rings$n > 0, ]

  # Zoom to the surface, the receivers that heard and the truth
  in_view <- rbind(hour_cells[c("x", "y")], heard[c("x", "y")],
                   hour_truth[c("x", "y")])
  xlim <- range(in_view$x) + c(-margin, margin)
  ylim <- range(in_view$y) + c(-margin, margin)

  # Take the water in view, coloured by depth with the ramp of
  # detfield::scale_fill_depth(). The fill scale holds the probability, so
  # the depth key is an alpha scale held at 1 whose boxes take the ramp
  depth_ramp <- scales::seq_gradient_pal("cornflowerblue", "blue4")
  water <- terra::as.data.frame(abs(lake), xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(water)[3] <- "depth_m"
  deepest <- max(water$depth_m)
  water$colour <- depth_ramp(water$depth_m / deepest)
  depth_breaks <- pretty(c(0, deepest), n = 3)
  depth_breaks <- depth_breaks[depth_breaks <= deepest]
  water <- water[water$x > xlim[1] - 100 & water$x < xlim[2] + 100 &
                   water$y > ylim[1] - 100 & water$y < ylim[2] + 100, ]

  # Draw the layers
  top_prob <- max(hour_cells$prob)
  cell_size <- terra::res(lake)[1]
  ggplot(hour_cells, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_tile(data = water, aes(fill = I(.data$colour), alpha = .data$depth_m),
              width = cell_size, height = cell_size) +
    scale_alpha_continuous(
      name = "Depth (m)", range = c(1, 1), limits = c(0, deepest),
      breaks = depth_breaks,
      guide = guide_legend(position = "bottom", nrow = 1, override.aes = list(
        fill = depth_ramp(depth_breaks / deepest)
      ))
    ) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = .data$prob), width = cell_size, height = cell_size) +
    detfield::scale_fill_probability(
      name = "Probability\nper cell", limits = c(0, top_prob),
      breaks = c(0, top_prob), labels = signif(c(0, top_prob), 2)
    ) +
    geom_path(data = outline, aes(group = interaction(.data$part, .data$hole),
                                  colour = "95% region"), linewidth = 0.9) +
    detfield::layer_receivers(rings, count = "n", size = 3, max_size = 9) +
    geom_point(data = hour_truth[hour_truth$n_detections == 0, ],
               aes(colour = "Not heard"), shape = 4, size = 1.6, stroke = 0.7) +
    geom_point(data = hour_truth[hour_truth$n_detections > 0, ],
               aes(colour = "Heard"), shape = 21, fill = "#2ECC40", size = 2,
               stroke = 0.3) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      name = NULL, breaks = c("95% region", "Heard", "Not heard"),
      values = c(`95% region` = "#00A087", Heard = "black", `Not heard` = "red3")
    ) +
    coord_equal(xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Animal %s, %s to %s UTC", animal,
                         format(hour, "%H:%M", tz = "UTC"),
                         format(hour + 3600, "%H:%M", tz = "UTC")),
         x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)") +
    detfield::annotation_scale_bar(location = "br") +
    detfield::theme_positionr()
}
```

Animal `r mapped_hour$animal_id` in the hour from
`r format(mapped_hour$bin_start, "%H:%M", tz = "UTC")` UTC is the animal-hour of Figure 1,
and the error of its surface mean is `r round(mapped_hour$error_mean_m)` m. The chunk below takes, of the same most-heard animal-hours, the
one with the lowest share of true positions inside its region, and maps it with `surface_map()`
(Figure 3).

```{r pick-a-poor-hour}
# Take the most-heard animal-hour with the lowest share inside its region
poor_hour <- most_heard[which.min(most_heard$in_region), ]
poor_hour
```

```{r poor-hour-guard, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
# Figure 3 must not draw the hour of Figure 1
stopifnot(poor_hour$animal_id != mapped_hour$animal_id ||
            poor_hour$bin_start != mapped_hour$bin_start)
```

```{r map-a-poor-hour, message = FALSE, fig.height = 5.4, fig.alt = "Location surface of a poorly placed animal-hour on Stoney Lake: magma cells over water drawn by depth, the 95% region outlined, yellow rings for the receivers that heard the animal, white rings for silent receivers, and the animal's true transmissions, most of them outside the region."}
# Map the poor hour from the surfaces of this section
surface_map(surfaces, poor_hour$animal_id, poor_hour$bin_start, lake,
            receivers, sim$detections, truth)
```

*Figure 3. Animal `r poor_hour$animal_id` from
`r format(poor_hour$bin_start, "%H:%M", tz = "UTC")` UTC, heard by
`r poor_hour$receivers_heard` receivers:
`r round(poor_hour$in_region * poor_hour$n_truth)` of its `r poor_hour$n_truth` true positions lie
inside the 95% region, and the surface mean is `r round(poor_hour$error_mean_m)` m from their
mean.*
